controls.title: Root user is protected (MFA on, no access keys)
controls.summary: not evaluated (the scanner returned no result - see Method)
controls.why: The root user can do everything, including closing the account. A stolen root password or key is a total loss.

fix.console: Sign in as root > Security credentials > assign an MFA device (passkey or hardware key); delete any root access keys. In AWS Organizations, turn on centralized root access management for member accounts.

controls.title: Every console user has MFA
controls.why: Passwords get phished and reused. MFA stops most account takeovers.

fix.cli: aws iam list-virtual-mfa-devices  # find users without a device, then enable MFA for each, or move people to IAM Identity Center
fix.console: IAM > Users > (user) > Security credentials > Assign MFA device.

controls.title: Access keys are rotated and unused keys removed
controls.why: Long-lived keys leak through laptops, CI logs and git history. Datadog found active keys over a year old at 59% of IAM users.

fix.cli:
aws iam update-access-key --user-name <user> --access-key-id <key> --status Inactive   # then delete once nothing breaks
aws iam delete-access-key --user-name <user> --access-key-id <key>

controls.title: People get permissions through groups, roles or SSO - not attached to users
controls.why: Permissions attached user by user drift and are never reviewed. Groups, roles and IAM Identity Center keep access auditable.

fix.cli: aws iam detach-user-policy --user-name <user> --policy-arn <arn>   # after adding the user to a group with the same rights
fix.console: Prefer IAM Identity Center: one login per person, permission sets per job, no long-lived keys.

controls.title: Full administrator rights are limited to a break-glass role
controls.why: Every identity with AdministratorAccess is a way to lose the whole account. Most teams need two or three, not ten.

fix.console: Replace AdministratorAccess with job-based policies (PowerUserAccess, ReadOnlyAccess, or service-scoped). Keep one MFA-protected break-glass role.

failing.message: AWS policy AdministratorAccess is attached and allows '*:*' administrative privileges.

controls.title: Password policy requires long, non-reused passwords
controls.why: Only matters for IAM users with console access, but auditors and customer questionnaires ask for it.

failing.message: IAM password policy does not require minimum length of 14 characters.
IAM password policy reuse prevention is less than 24 or not set.

controls.title: IAM Access Analyzer watches for external access
controls.summary: not evaluated (the scanner returned no result - see Method)
controls.why: It flags buckets, roles and keys shared with other accounts or the public - for free.

controls.title: CloudTrail records every region, with tamper-evident, private logs
controls.why: Without CloudTrail there is no record of who did what - no investigation, and no basis for a breach report.
dpdp_areas: Logging and monitoring (logs kept at least one year)

fix.terraform: module.security_baseline: cloudtrail = true   # multi-region trail, log-file validation, private encrypted bucket
fix.cli:
aws cloudtrail create-trail --name org-trail --s3-bucket-name <bucket> --is-multi-region-trail --enable-log-file-validation
aws cloudtrail start-logging --name org-trail

failing.message: No CloudTrail trails enabled with logging were found.

controls.title: GuardDuty threat detection is on
controls.summary: not evaluated (the scanner returned no result - see Method)
controls.why: GuardDuty spots stolen credentials, crypto-mining and unusual API calls. Costs a few dollars a month for small accounts.

controls.title: AWS Config records configuration changes
controls.why: Config keeps a history of how each resource was configured - the evidence auditors and investigators ask for.
dpdp_areas: Logging and monitoring (logs kept at least one year)

fix.console: AWS Config > Get started > record all resources > deliver to the CloudTrail logs bucket.

controls.title: Log groups keep logs for at least a year
controls.why: Logs kept for days or weeks are gone when an incident is found months later. One year is the minimum many customers - and India's DPDP Rules - expect for security logs. ('Never expire' passes here; the cost check LOGS-001 flags its price.)
dpdp_areas: Logging and monitoring (logs kept at least one year)

fix.cli: bash aws-foundation/fix-pack/scripts/set-log-retention.sh --days 365   # dry run first; add --apply to change

controls.title: Spend alerts would catch abuse within a day
controls.why: A stolen key used for crypto-mining shows up first on the bill. Budgets with email alerts are free.

failing.message: No budget with an alert: abuse of a stolen key would only show up on the monthly bill

controls.title: S3 Block Public Access is on for the whole account
controls.why: One account-wide switch stops any bucket from being made public by mistake - the cause of many data leaks.

failing.message: Block Public Access is not configured for the account 453348321107.

controls.title: No bucket is public
controls.why: Public buckets are found by automated scanners within hours.

fix.cli:
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket <bucket> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true
# if the bucket serves a website, put CloudFront with origin access control in front instead

failing.message: S3 Bucket acme-demo-453348321107-uploads has public access due to bucket policy.

controls.title: Data is encrypted by default (S3 and EBS)
controls.why: Default encryption is free and protects disks, snapshots and buckets that get copied or shared by mistake.

failing.message: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.

controls.title: Databases are encrypted, private, backed up and protected from deletion
controls.summary: no matching resources in the scanned regions
controls.why: An RDS instance reachable from the internet, without backups, is one mistake away from a data leak or permanent loss.

fix.cli:
aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier <db> --backup-retention-period 7 --deletion-protection --no-publicly-accessible --apply-immediately
# encryption at rest needs a new instance: snapshot -> copy with --kms-key-id -> restore -> switch over

controls.title: No snapshot is public
controls.summary: no matching resources in the scanned regions
controls.why: A public EBS or RDS snapshot hands a full copy of the disk or database to anyone.

fix.cli:
aws ec2 modify-snapshot-attribute --snapshot-id <snap> --attribute createVolumePermission --operation-type remove --group-names all
aws rds modify-db-snapshot-attribute --db-snapshot-identifier <snap> --attribute-name restore --values-to-remove all

controls.title: No SSH, RDP or database port is open to the whole internet
controls.why: Open admin and database ports are scanned constantly; one weak password or unpatched service is enough.

fix.cli:
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id <sg> --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
# use SSM Session Manager (no open port) or a VPN/allow-list instead

controls.title: Default security groups allow no traffic
controls.summary: no matching resources in the scanned regions
controls.why: Resources launched without a chosen group land in the default one; it should block everything.

fix.terraform: module.security_baseline: default_security_group_vpc_ids = ["vpc-..."]   # check nothing uses the group first

controls.title: Instances require IMDSv2
controls.why: IMDSv1 lets an SSRF bug in a web app read the instance's cloud credentials (the Capital One breach). Datadog found IMDSv2 enforced on only 49% of instances.

fix.cli:
bash aws-foundation/fix-pack/scripts/require-imdsv2.sh --regions <region>   # dry run lists instances; --apply after testing one
aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --instance-id <id> --http-tokens required --http-put-response-hop-limit 2

controls.title: Only intended instances have public IP addresses
controls.why: Every public instance is attack surface (and costs $3.65 a month per IPv4 address). Most belong behind a load balancer.

fix.console: Move workloads to private subnets behind a load balancer; reach them with SSM Session Manager. Keep a public IP only where it is intended, and note it in the report.

controls.title: No secrets in Lambda variables, EC2 user data or launch templates
controls.why: Anyone with read-only access - including auditors and many SaaS tools - can read these fields.

fix.console: Move each value to Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString), read it at runtime, then rotate it - it must be treated as exposed.

controls.title: CI/CD logs in with short-lived OIDC credentials, not stored keys
controls.summary: not evaluated (the scanner returned no result - see Method)
controls.why: Keys stored in CI were stolen in the tj-actions, Trivy and Checkmarx incidents. OIDC tokens expire in minutes.

fix.console: Create an OIDC role trusted only by your repository's main branch or a protected environment, switch the workflow to role-to-assume, then delete the old access key.
